correctness.rationale: From the definition, a \(3\)-layered \(n\) has \(I(n)\ge3\). The exchange inequality makes the finite exponent-partition maxima rigorous. Explicit complete divisor partitions prove all survivors are \(3\)-layered; `verify.py` independently replays the exact arithmetic and partition certificates.

value.rationale: \(\Omega(n)=5\) is the first arithmetically possible multiplicity layer for \(3\)-layered numbers. Classifying it exactly is a natural boundary problem, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The result both explains the sharp lower bound and separates the broader divisor-partition class from triperfect numbers by four explicit non-triperfect boundary members.
